description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT against DataCanvas tables staged by fx_get_timeseries. Supports aggregations, GROUP BY, window functions, and JOINs across multiple registered tables. Run fx_dataframe_describe first to discover table names and column schemas. Requires DataCanvas, which is on by default — a deployment that turns it off does not list this tool at all, and fx_get_timeseries returns every range inline there.

canvas_id.description: Canvas ID returned by fx_get_timeseries. Re-run fx_get_timeseries to obtain a fresh canvas_id if this one has expired.

query.description: Read-only SQL SELECT statement. Reference tables by the names returned by fx_dataframe_describe or the table_name field from fx_get_timeseries. Example: SELECT date, rate FROM <table_name> WHERE date > '2024-01-01' ORDER BY date; replace <table_name> with the returned name, including its unique suffix.

row_limit.description: Most rows to return (positive integer, default 150; values above 10000 clamp to 10000 with a notice). When the query produces more, truncated is true — page with ORDER BY <column> LIMIT <n> OFFSET <m> in the SQL, or aggregate, rather than raising this toward the maximum.

name: fx_dataframe_query

canvas_id.description: The canvas ID used — pass to a subsequent fx_dataframe_query or fx_dataframe_describe call.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `canvas_not_found`: canvas_id does not exist or has been evicted. `missing_table`: The SQL references a table that is not staged on this canvas, or whose TTL expired. `invalid_query`: SQL is not a SELECT, references unknown columns, or has a syntax error. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Reports requested and effective row limits when clamped, and the ORDER BY … LIMIT … OFFSET query shape when the result is truncated.

row_count.description: Rows returned — always the length of rows. When truncated is true this equals row_limit, not the full result size.

rows.description: Result rows, at most row_limit (default 150). Each key is a column name from the query.

items.description: One result row — column-name → value pairs matching the SELECT columns.

truncated.description: True when the query produced more rows than row_limit and rows holds only the first row_limit of them. Fetch the rest with ORDER BY <column> LIMIT <n> OFFSET <m> — ORDER BY is required for deterministic paging — or aggregate to shrink the result.

title: Fx Dataframe Query
